transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton. The FAA says it will temporarily stop
using the types of routers involved in the technical meltdown that caused a nationwide
ground stop last week, as NPR's Joe Hernandez reports transportation officials say they're
still investigating what went wrong. The government contractor L3Harris was installing the router at
a site in Arkansas just before the technical disruptions began. Transportation Secretary
Sean Duffy said 68 of these routers had been installed previously without incident.
This is the one that started to behave this way. So we thought it's only prudent to pause the use
of these routers. L3Harris sent the routers involved in Friday's incident to its lab in Florida,
where officials with the FAA and the FBI are also on site. Duffy says there's no indication the
malfunction was the result of a cyber attack, but that the investigation is ongoing. Joe Hernandez,
NPR News. Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong signaled interest in returning to lead the
computer chip company after he resigned following revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese
spy. But NVIDIA's board chair says the company does not intend to reinstate him. Wong has agreed
to appear before Congress. NPR's Shannon Bond reports he'll face scrutiny over national security
scandals swirling around the company. Jensen Wong and NVIDIA's top lawyer will answer questions from
the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees and the Select Committee on the
Chinese Communist Party in early December. The interviews will take place behind closed doors.
Lawmakers say they want answers about NVIDIA's role in alleged chip smuggling and efforts to
evade export controls meant to block China from accessing the most advanced U.S. chips.
And they'll ask Wong about his involvement with a woman U.S. intelligence officials say
was recruited by China's top spy agency. NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.
Shannon Bond, NPR News. In North Carolina, Democrat Raymond Smith has defeated Republican
congressman Greg Murphy in a tight U.S. House race. That's according to a race call by the
Associated Press. As NPR's Hansi Lo Wong reports, it's the latest example of the midterm blue wave
and helps offset a drop in the number of Black House members in the next Congress. Former
Democratic state lawmaker Raymond Smith flipped North Carolina's third congressional district
with just a few hundred votes. Smith's victory brings the total number of Black members of the
U.S. House to at least 61. That's according to an NPR analysis of the latest AP race calls,
and that's down from 63 currently. It's also just two away from the record loss of four Black
representatives around the end of Reconstruction. Some redistricting experts warn that in the coming
years, more Black-represented districts may be eliminated when voting maps are redrawn
because of the Supreme Court's weakening of the Voting Rights Act's protections against
racial discrimination in redistricting. Hansi Lo Wong, NPR News. The U.S. stock market dropped
again as NVIDIA and other jittery A.I. stocks led widespread losses on Wall Street. It's NPR.
President Trump's Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza ceasefire between Israel and Hamas delivered
a bleak report on its progress to the U.N. Security Council today. The report warns that continued
delays will doom the chances of restoring peace and stability. Israel has continued to launch
deadly strikes and block humanitarian aid. The board says people in Gaza are set to face "another
winter intense and rubble." New treatments like immunotherapy and stepped-up screening continue
to improve survival from lung cancer, though it's still the top cancer killer, NPR's Yuki Naguchi
reports. The American Lung Association's annual report finds 31 percent of lung cancer patients
are still living five years after diagnosis. That compares with 18 percent nine years ago.
The report speaks to rapid development in new treatments that target genetic mutations that
drive cancer or immunotherapies that combat it. New technologies like biomarker testing have also
enabled treatment to become more personalized. The survey found low-dose CT scanning rates
increasing, but still below a quarter of those eligible. Low smoking rates have also reduced
incidence of lung cancer, but about 230,000 Americans will be diagnosed this year.
Yuki Naguchi, NPR News. Miami is preparing for the much-anticipated arrival of the Grand Theft Auto
6 video game, which is set in Miami-inspired Vice City. The Miami Heat basketball team will wear
black-and-pink Vice City jerseys tomorrow. The game's developer, Rockstar, commissioned a series
of murals, many in the Wynwood neighborhood, known worldwide for its street art. This is NPR.
This message comes from NPR sponsor Charles Schwab with its original podcast Schwab Market Update.

topics.text: FAA pauses use of L3Harris routers after nationwide ground stop, cause still under investigation
Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong to face closed-door congressional questioning in early December
Democrat Raymond Smith defeats Republican Greg Murphy in North Carolina's third congressional district
U.S. stock market falls again as NVIDIA and other A.I. stocks lead widespread losses
Trump's Board of Peace reports to U.N. Security Council that Gaza ceasefire progress is stalled
American Lung Association report shows improved lung cancer survival rates but persistent low screening
Miami prepares for Grand Theft Auto 6 release with Heat Vice City jerseys and Wynwood murals
